verdict.rationale: Stripe documents its own fiat-to-crypto onramp. It comes as a Stripe-hosted page, an Embedded onramp for websites and an embedded mobile SDK, with Stripe acting as merchant of record and handling KYC, so end users can buy inside the developer's product. Bridge also documents programmatic on-ramps. However, the evidence speaks of 'cryptocurrencies' generally rather than stablecoins specifically, and never names the funding methods. Missing for 10: explicit documentation that stablecoins (e.g. USDC) are purchasable via the onramp, documented card and bank-transfer funding methods, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can embed a fiat-to-stablecoin onramp — a documented widget or API where end users buy stablecoins with cards or bank transfers inside my product

citations.quote: The Stripe fiat-to-crypto onramp lets your customers securely purchase and exchange cryptocurrencies directly from your platform or decentralized application (Dapp) at checkout.
Use the Embedded onramp to let your customers check out directly in your website.
Use the Embedded components onramp (mobile SDK) to let your customers check out directly in your application.
Stripe acts as the merchant of record for these onramp transactions and assumes full liability for all fraud and disputes.
Programmatically support on-ramps, off-ramps, and crypto-to-crypto flows.
